title: Photosynthesis (KS4 Biology)
subject: Biology
strapline: How plants make their own food using light energy.
facts: Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction: it takes in energy (from light).
Word equation: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (using light energy and chlorophyll).
It happens in the chloroplasts, which contain the green pigment chlorophyll that absorbs light.
The glucose made is used for respiration, or converted to starch for storage, or to cellulose, proteins and fats.
The rate of photosynthesis is affected by light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature.
These are called limiting factors — the one in shortest supply caps the rate.
Too high a temperature slows the reaction because the enzymes involved denature.

quick_quiz.q: What are the two reactants in photosynthesis?
In which part of the cell does photosynthesis happen?
Name a limiting factor of photosynthesis.
quick_quiz.a: light intensity (or CO₂ concentration, or temperature)

teacher_tips: Insist on the full word equation with light and chlorophyll named.
Use graphs of rate vs each factor to teach "limiting factor".
Connect to respiration as the reverse energy story.
